name: Price
descr: The commercial half of a goods: what it costs and how many there are - the prices with their currencies, the supplier, the discount group, the tax group, the stock and the counts on the warehouses, the auto-count, and the parameters standing on it. The right is for_price, given out in the program on the sections a goods hangs in, so only goods hanging in a section of yours are reached here. The other half - the names and the texts a buyer reads - belongs to the Description tool.

commands.name: CmdTopic
commands.descr:
Walks the goods of the sections named - the plain way to see what stands where. Searching by the columns of the map is CmdQuery.

Name the sections in topic_id, and topic_sub takes the whole branch under each of them; the Catalog tool answers the tree to pick them from. A section this person may not price is walked past, whatever the call names.

The goods come by id, and so does every page of them: a walk of many pages loses none and says none twice. Where a goods stands and at what place comes with it, in the rows of topic_store - sort by that if the order of the shop is what is wanted.

A goods hanging in several of the sections walked is answered once. The answer is the one CmdQuery gives: the goods, the sections they hang in, their parameters, their counts on the warehouses - and found, the whole count of what stands there, whatever the page asked for.

params.name: topic_id
params.descr: the sections to walk, and nothing outside them

params.name: topic_sub
params.descr: true - the whole branch under every section named is walked with it

params.name: limit
params.descr: how many goods of the ones standing there to answer with; found says how many there are in all, so a page is chosen knowing the size

params.name: offset
params.descr: how many of the goods found to step over before this page - 100 takes the second page of a hundred

commands.name: CmdQuery
commands.descr:
Finds the goods by a query written as json and answers them with everything that hangs on them - the goods, the sections they hang in, their parameters, their counts on the warehouses.

ASKED FOR NOTHING - an empty query, or none at all - it answers its own signature instead: every table with every column and its type, and what may be asked of each. Nothing outside that list is taken, so a first call asks for it and the ones after are built by it.

THE SHAPE. A query starts from the root table of the sign and holds a list of conditions. A list is an AND, always. Four things may stand in it:
a condition - {"field": "price", "op": "between", "value": [1000, 5000]};
an or - {"or": [ ..., ... ]};
a not - {"not": ...}, of one condition or of one nested table;
a nested table - {"topic_store": [ ... ]}, which means THERE IS such a row: every condition inside it holds on one and the same row. A table goes one level deep only, and only a table the sign marks nest.

THE SECTIONS are a nested table like any other: {"topic_store": [{"field": "topic_id", "op": "in", "value": [9, 10]}]}. The sections are named as they are - a whole branch is named section by section, and the Catalog tool answers the tree to build such a list from.

NOTHING STANDS BESIDE THE ROOT TABLE. The page is a field of the call - limit and offset - and the goods come by id, page after page, so a walk of many pages loses none and says none twice. Sorting them any other way is done by whoever reads the answer. Whatever the page, the answer carries found - the whole count of what matched - so the size of a search is known without pulling it.

THE OPERATIONS come from the type of the column, and the sign names them: eq, in, between, ge, le for numbers, eq, between, ge, le for days, eq, in, like for words, eq for flags. between takes two values, in takes a list, the rest take one. like looks for a part of the text anywhere in it.

AN EXAMPLE of the whole thing:
{"store": [
  {"field": "no_visible", "op": "eq", "value": false},
  {"field": "price", "op": "between", "value": [1000, 5000]},
  {"or": [ {"field": "status_key", "op": "in", "value": ["kExist", "kExistOrder"]},
            {"field": "how", "op": "ge", "value": 1} ]},
  {"topic_store": [ {"field": "topic_id", "op": "in", "value": [9, 10, 11]} ]},
  {"store_param": [ {"field": "param_id", "op": "eq", "value": 1},
                    {"field": "value_id", "op": "eq", "value": 2} ]},
  {"not": {"store_stock": [ {"field": "provider_stock_id", "op": "eq", "value": 9},
                            {"field": "how", "op": "eq", "value": 0} ]}}
]}

The goods of a list of ids are asked for the same way: {"store": [ {"field": "id", "op": "in", "value": [25, 26]} ]}.

The right stands beside the query and is not part of it: only the goods hanging in a section this person may price are ever met, whatever the query says. The place a goods keeps in a section is answered here but never written - the Place tool shapes that.

params.name: query
params.descr: the query itself, as the shape above; left out or empty, the command answers what may be named in one

params.name: limit
params.descr: how many goods of the ones found to answer with; found says how many there are in all, so a page is chosen knowing the size

params.name: offset
params.descr: how many of the goods found to step over before this page - 100 takes the second page of a hundred

commands.name: CmdAdd
commands.descr: Adds a goods and hangs it in the section at once - a goods hanging nowhere is seen by the Lost tool alone. Every column of the half may come in the same call, and what the call does not name a fresh goods is born with: the days stamped now, hidden from the storefront, out of stock, of the plain kind and the plain view. The section must be yours to price.

commands.name: CmdParamAdd
commands.descr: Sets a parameter on goods: one row of store_param on each of them. A value of the parameter's own list goes by value_id, a value of your own by value_name. A goods already carrying that parameter takes a second row - read first if that matters.

params.name: store_id
params.descr: id of the goods, or several of them

params.name: param_id
params.descr: id of the parameter to set - the Parameters tool answers them

params.name: value_id
params.descr: id of the value of that parameter, when it keeps a list of them

params.name: value_name
params.descr: a value of your own, when the parameter allows one

params.name: value_set_sum
params.descr: the sum this value carries

params.name: value_curr_id
params.descr: id of the currency of that sum

params.name: pos
params.descr: the place of the row among the parameters of that goods; left out, a row takes its own id

commands.name: CmdParamUpdate
commands.descr: Changes the columns given of the rows of store_param; a row keeps whatever the call leaves out. CmdTopic and CmdQuery answer the rows of a goods with their ids. Only the id of a row is fixed: store_id moves the row to another goods and param_id makes it another parameter, and a goods it moves to is weighed by the same right.

params.name: id
params.descr: id of the row of store_param, or several of them

params.name: store_id
params.descr: moves the row to another goods; that goods is weighed by the same right

params.name: param_id
params.descr: moves the row to another parameter of the shop

params.name: value_id
params.descr: id of the value of that parameter, when it keeps a list of them

params.name: value_name
params.descr: a value of your own, when the parameter allows one

params.name: value_set_sum
params.descr: the sum this value carries

params.name: value_curr_id
params.descr: id of the currency of that sum

params.name: pos
params.descr: the place of the row among the parameters of that goods; a row is born standing at its own id

commands.name: CmdParamRemove
commands.descr: Deletes the rows of store_param by id. The parameter itself stays in the store and the goods keeps its other parameters.

params.name: id
params.descr: id of the row of store_param, or several of them

commands.name: CmdStockAdd
commands.descr: Puts goods on a warehouse: one row of store_stock on each of the goods named, with the count they hold there. The warehouses themselves belong to the Providers tool, and it answers their ids. A goods already standing on that warehouse takes a second row - read first if that matters.

params.name: store_id
params.descr: the goods to put on the warehouse

params.name: provider_stock_id
params.descr: the warehouse they stand on - the Providers tool answers the warehouses

params.name: how
params.descr: how many of the goods stand there

params.name: params
params.descr: a word of the shop about this row, kept as it comes

commands.name: CmdStockUpdate
commands.descr: Changes the columns given of store_stock rows, by id - CmdTopic and CmdQuery answer them with their ids. A row keeps whatever the call leaves out. Only the id of a row is fixed: store_id moves the row to another goods, weighed by the same right, and provider_stock_id moves it to another warehouse.

params.name: id
params.descr: the rows of store_stock to change

params.name: store_id
params.descr: moves the row to another goods; that goods is weighed by the same right

params.name: provider_stock_id
params.descr: moves the row to another warehouse

params.name: how
params.descr: how many of the goods stand there

params.name: params
params.descr: a word of the shop about this row

commands.name: CmdStockRemove
commands.descr: Deletes store_stock rows by id. The goods and the warehouse stay as they are; only the count on that warehouse is gone.

params.name: id
params.descr: the rows of store_stock to delete
